turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil said that the presence of Sandip and his followers in his territory was an affront to his authority, and that he would not tolerate it any longer.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if his concerns about the Mussulmans were also related to his own estate, and if there were any other issues he was worried about.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Bimala that the situation with the Mussulmans was indeed a concern for his estate as well, but his main worry was the lawlessness and disregard for authority that Sandip's presence seemed to encourage.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he believed that the lawlessness in his estate was directly caused by Sandip's presence, or if there were other factors at play.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil pointedly told Bimala that the lack of authority Sandip displayed was a symptom of a broader problem in the region, one that needed to be addressed before it was too late.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip scoffed at Nikhil's warnings, saying that he was more concerned about the state of Nikhil's own estate, which seemed to be falling into disrepair under his management.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his estate's problems were a mere fraction of the region's overall woes, and that he would not stand idly by while the situation continued to deteriorate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip retorted that Nikhil's estate was indeed a mess, but at least it wasn't a haven for cutthroats and ne'er-do-wells, like some places he could mention.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil sternly warned Sandip that his flippant attitude would only exacerbate the situation, and that he should take immediate action to address the growing unrest in the region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was more concerned about the safety of his own property, and that he wouldn't let Nikhil's dire warnings scare him into making a fool of himself.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil turned to Bimala, his expression stern, and told her that she should be aware of the situation and take precautions for their own safety, as well as for the safety of their estate.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to clarify the specific steps he thought Sandip should take to address the growing unrest, her voice calm and measured.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip must take concrete measures to protect his property and people, and that merely relying on his own security forces was not sufficient to address the growing threat.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil what he was planning to do about the situation, other than lecturing him on it, and if he had any brilliant solutions to share.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip if he had any regard for the welfare of his own people, or if he was merely intent on ignoring the danger that threatened their safety

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed, a low, mocking sound, and told Nikhil that he was starting to sound like a character from a Bengali melodrama, always warning of impending doom and destruction.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's tone turned stern as he told Sandip that his flippant attitude was a dereliction of his duty as a zamindar

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he seemed to have lost all sense of proportion, always expecting him to swoon at the mere mention of danger, and that it was rather tiresome.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil said that he would not stand idly by while Sandip ignored the warnings and put the lives of his people at risk

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was beginning to suspect that his warnings were merely a cover for his own lack of initiative, that a true leader would take action, not just prattle on about danger.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
